before.quote:
Let $f(x,\mu)$ be $C^2$ on an open set in $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^p$, let $q=(x,\mu)$, and set $g(q)=(f(x,\mu),0_p)$. Write $Pq=x$. For each fixed $\mu$, let $\Phi_\theta(q)$ be the time-$\theta$ flow of $q'=g(q)$, so its parameter coordinates remain constant. For an affine phase $\psi(x)=c^\top(x-x_{\rm ref})$, define
$$
G(q,\theta)=\begin{bmatrix}P\Phi_\theta(q)-Pq\\\psi(Pq)\end{bmatrix}.
$$
For $p=0$ this is the shooting residual in [[def-phase-bordered-periodic-orbit-bvp]]. Its Jacobian is
$$
DG(q,\theta)=\begin{bmatrix}P\mathcal M-P& f(P\Phi_\theta(q),\mu)\\ c^\top P&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal M=D_q\Phi_\theta(q).
$$

For a rational box $Q=X\times\Lambda\times\Theta$ with $\Theta\subset(0,\infty)$, a **validated shooting jet enclosure** consists of: (i) a box containing $P\Phi_\theta(q)$ for every $q,\theta$ in the input; (ii) a box containing the residual $G(Q)$; (iii) an interval matrix $J(Q)$ containing every $DG(q,\theta)$; and (iv) trajectory and monodromy boxes containing every scaled trajectory $P\Phi_{\theta s}(q)$, $0\le s\le1$, and the physical-state block of $\mathcal M$. The boxes use [[def-real-boxes-and-interval-jacobian-enclosures]] and [[lem-real-interval-arithmetic-preserves-enclosure]]. The exact derivative formula follows from [[prop-shooting-residual-derivative]], and its flow sensitivity is on the common tube of [[lem-c1-ode-flow-on-common-tube]]. A finite success record is admissible only when obtained by the range-oracle procedure of [[alg-validated-euler-flow-and-monodromy-enclosure]], whose exact flow and monodromy enclosure is guaranteed by [[thm-validated-euler-flow-and-monodromy-enclosure-soundness]], with all queries and interval operations successful and outward under [[def-verified-flow-variational-range-oracle]]. For this call instantiate that procedure and its soundness theorem with state dimension $n=d+p$, initial state box $X\times\Lambda$, field $g(q)=(f(x,\mu),0_p)$, and period interval $\Theta$. Its augmented field is $H_g(q,Z,\theta)=(\theta g(q),\theta Dg(q)Z,0)$ with $Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$; the supplied range provider is for this $H_g$ on its actual compact convex rational tube $K_g\subset\mathbb R^{n+n^2+1}$. Initialize $Y_0=(X\times\Lambda)\times\{I_n\}\times\Theta$ and require every Euler tube query and inclusion check in this same $K_g$ to succeed. Retain the full $n\times n$ endpoint variation enclosure for $\mathcal M=D_q\Phi_\theta(q)$ when forming $P\mathcal M-P$: its first $d$ rows include both the state and parameter sensitivity columns, while its lower parameter rows are $(0,I_p)$ because the parameters are constant. The physical monodromy is the first $d$ rows and first $d$ columns of $\mathcal M$.

To enclose the period column, let $X_T$ be the first $d$ coordinate projection of the successful endpoint enclosure $Y_N$. The exact augmented endpoint lies in $X_T\times\Lambda$: its parameter equals its initial value in $\Lambda$, even if a returned interval coordinate is wider. Form the rational query box $Q_T=(X_T\times\Lambda)\times\{I_n\}\times\Theta$ and check $Q_T\subseteq K_g$ before requesting $H_g^\#(Q_T)$ from that same supplied provider. If the inclusion or query fails, return inconclusive. The first $d$ entries of its vector-field block enclose every $\theta f(P\Phi_\theta(q),\mu)$; divide these entries outward by the positive interval $\Theta$ to enclose the entire period column. Thus the query includes every admitted parameter and the matching augmented identity. For $p=0$, $n=d$ and the parameter factor is the singleton empty tuple, giving the fixed-parameter construction. These residual/Jacobian boxes are in the named coordinate order $(q,\theta)=(x,\mu,\theta)$; a section callback whose variables are ordered $(x,\theta,\mu)$ applies that fixed column permutation before appending its affine section row. Any unavailable query or inclusion returns inconclusive. A finite Newton, multiple-shooting, or collocation residual alone is not a validated jet enclosure.

before.quote:
Input a positive integer $n$, a nonempty complex matrix family $\mathcal M$ enclosed entrywise by finite dyadic real/imaginary rectangles, a dyadic center matrix $M_0$, a certified dyadic bound $\delta_A\ge\sup_{M\in\mathcal M}\|M-M_0\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$, and a simple positively oriented strictly convex polygon $\Gamma$ with dyadic vertices and filled interior $P$. Supply the dyadic disk cover and point preconditioners required by [[alg-complex-resolvent-cover-validator]], a positive integer $N$ for midpoint subdivisions of each edge, a positive integer $K_\pi$ for the arctangent series, and a finite arithmetic budget. The family may be the monodromy block of a validated shooting jet; no correlation between matrix entries is required. A complex rectangle here is the product of one closed dyadic real interval and one closed dyadic imaginary interval for each matrix entry.

1. Write the ordered dyadic vertices as $v_0,\ldots,v_{r-1}$, with indices modulo $r$. Require $r\ge3$, pairwise distinct vertices, and, for every $i$ and every $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$, the exact rational determinant $\operatorname{Im}(\overline{(v_{i+1}-v_i)}(v_k-v_i))>0$. Each directed edge is then an exposed edge of the convex hull; since there are $r$ such edges and $r$ distinct vertices, they form its simple counterclockwise boundary. If any test fails, output `inconclusive`. Then run the resolvent-cover validator on every edge for the entire family. If any segment is uncovered, an outward inequality is not strict, or no finite upper bound $M_R$ on $\|(zI-M)^{-1}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$ is returned, output `inconclusive`.
2. Subdivide each oriented edge $e_j=b_j-a_j$ into $N$ equal parts, with rational midpoints $z_{jk}=a_j+(k+1/2)e_j/N$. By exact rational complex elimination, compute $R^0_{jk}=(z_{jk}I-M_0)^{-1}$; a singular center matrix or an incomplete operation returns `inconclusive`. For each rational complex entry $a+ib$ of $R^0_{jk}$, use rational square-root bisection to find an upper bound for $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, then sum row bounds to obtain $b_{jk}\ge\|R^0_{jk}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$. Use the same bisection to obtain $s_j\ge|e_j|$. If the finite budget does not produce these rational bounds, return `inconclusive`.
3. Form the exact center midpoint sum
$$S_0=\sum_j\frac{e_j}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\operatorname{tr}R^0_{jk},$$
and the outward error allowance
$$E=\frac{n M_R^2}{2N}\sum_j|e_j|^2+\frac{n M_R\delta_A}{N}\sum_{j,k}s_jb_{jk}.$$
The first term uses the exact rational squared modulus of each rational edge; the second uses the rational upper edge length $s_j$. The first term bounds midpoint quadrature error; the second bounds replacing each family resolvent by the center resolvent. All sums and products are exact rationals; if a required rational square-root upper bound is unavailable, return `inconclusive`.
4. Enclose $\pi$ using $\pi=4\arctan(1)$ and the alternating partial sum $4\sum_{k=0}^{K_\pi-1}(-1)^k/(2k+1)$ with tail radius $4/(2K_\pi+1)$. Require a positive lower endpoint. Using exact rational endpoint arithmetic, enclose $S_0/(2\pi i)$ and inflate its real and imaginary intervals by $E/(2\pi_{\rm low})$; call the resulting rectangle $I$.
5. Choose an integer $c$ and return `certified-count(c)` only if $0\le c\le n$, $\operatorname{Re}I\subset(c-1/2,c+1/2)$, $\operatorname{Im}I\subset(-1/2,1/2)$, and $0\in\operatorname{Im}I$. Otherwise return `inconclusive`. This operation counts roots with algebraic multiplicity in $\operatorname{int}P$ for every matrix in the supplied family; it does not classify a cluster touching the unit circle as stable or unstable.

For a simple separated multiplier, an optional left/right-conditioned finite enclosure may also be reported using [[lem-separated-simple-floquet-multiplier-perturbation-bound]]. The contour count remains the required path for clusters or unresolved individual eigenvectors.

The matrix family may be taken from the monodromy block of [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]]. Resolvent bounds use the complex infinity norm [[def-complex-infinity-matrix-norm]] and its product inequality [[lem-complex-infinity-matrix-norm-submultiplicative]]; the boundary cover is interpreted by [[thm-complex-resolvent-cover-validator-soundness]]. Root counting uses [[thm-argument-principle-null-homologous-cycle]], the inside/outside polygon index [[lem-positive-convex-polygon-winding-index]], and the determinant derivative [[thm-determinant-differential-and-jacobis-formula]]. The root multiplicities are those of the characteristic polynomial by [[thm-complex-polynomial-has-exactly-degree-many-roots-counted-with-multiplicity]]. The rational $\pi$ enclosure uses [[thm-principal-inverse-tangent-calculus]] and [[thm-alternating-series-test]].

For a state dimension $d\ge1$, the vector-field input is a $C^2$ map $f:U\to\mathbb R^d$ in fixed-parameter mode or a $C^2$ one-parameter family $f:U\times V\to\mathbb R^d$ with scalar parameter $\mu\in V\subset\mathbb R$ in section mode, where $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $V\subset\mathbb R$ are open. Also supply an affine phase with rational covector and reference point, a compact convex validation tube, and the sound range provider of [[def-verified-flow-variational-range-oracle]]. Supply positive finite step counts for each requested validated jet run, finite arithmetic and candidate-update budgets, a rational initial candidate, a dyadic point preconditioner $C$, a rational inverse witness $W$, a positive rational minimum box width $\eta$, and a finite Krawczyk box budget. In fixed-parameter mode the rational candidate box is $Z=X\times\Theta\subset U\times(0,\infty)$ with the parameter held fixed, so both the variable $z=(x,\theta)$ and residual $F=G$ have dimension $d+1$. In section mode require exactly one scalar continuation parameter $\mu\in\mathbb R$ (the $p=1$ case of [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]]), take $Z=X\times\Theta\times\Lambda$ with rational $\Lambda\subset V\subset\mathbb R$, and set $z=(x,\theta,\mu)$. Then $G$ has dimension $d+1$, the affine section adds one scalar equation, and both $z$ and $F$ have dimension $d+2$. All rational point and matrix operations below are exact or return an explicit arithmetic-failure status within the supplied cap.

Write $F=G$ in fixed-parameter mode. In **section mode**, used for continuation, require one scalar continuation parameter $\mu\in\mathbb R$ and write $z=(x,\theta,\mu)$ and $F(z)=(G(x,\theta,\mu),\tau^\top(z-z_p))$, where $G$ is the parameterized map in [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]], $\tau$ is a supplied unit normal, and $z_p$ is a supplied predictor. Supply certified rational enclosures for the coefficients and constant term of this affine row at every requested accuracy; if they are rational use their exact values, and otherwise use outward interval arithmetic. If a finite row enclosure cannot be obtained within the arithmetic cap, return inconclusive. For the one-parameter field use the static-parameter augmentation $g(x,\mu)=(f(x,\mu),0)$ in that definition and supply its sound augmented range provider and tube. Append a sound outward enclosure of the affine section row to every residual and Jacobian enclosure (the exact row when its data are rational). In fixed-parameter mode, $z=(x,\theta)$ and $F=G$ both have dimension $d+1$; in section mode, $z=(x,\theta,\mu)$ and $F=(G,\tau^\top(z-z_p))$ both have dimension $d+2$.

The procedure retains the following candidate modes; candidate generation alone never validates a root.

1. **Enclosure-guided single shooting:** this mode needs only the supplied range provider, not a pointwise differentiable numerical IVP evaluator. Start at the supplied rational $z_0\in Z$. At each of at most the supplied number of updates, run the validated shooting-jet procedure of [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]] on the singleton $\{z_k\}$, using its validated Euler method and the supplied finite caps. If a tube, range, domain or arithmetic check fails, return its inconclusive status and the last candidate. Otherwise let $r_k$ and $A_k$ be the coordinatewise rational midpoints of the returned boxes for $F(z_k)$ and $DF(z_k)$. Record $z_k$ as a candidate and attempt the independent validation below. If it does not validate and updates remain, call [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]] on $(A_k,r_k)$. A singular matrix returns singular-jacobian; otherwise its rational correction $u_k$ proposes $z_{k+1}=z_k+u_k$. Reject a proposal outside $Z$ with invalid-trial. The midpoint matrix is only a proposal matrix: it is not claimed to be the exact derivative of a numerical residual map. Exhaustion returns the last candidate and candidate-budget-exhausted.
2. **Differentiable single shooting:** supply, as an additional input for this mode, a certified differentiable evaluator satisfying [[def-certified-ivp-approximation-and-sensitivity-interface]] for the augmented BVP, including its approximate trajectories, $C^1$ endpoint map, exact numerical-map derivative, and uniform trajectory-error bound. Run [[alg-single-shooting-for-nonlinear-bvps]] on the phase-bordered BVP. In section mode augment the state by the constant parameter and append the affine section condition to its boundary residual. An interval jet alone is not this additional evaluator; if it is absent, return evaluator-unavailable without making the call.
3. **Discretized candidate:** either run [[alg-multiple-shooting-for-nonlinear-bvps]] on the augmented segment BVP with separately supplied certified differentiable segment evaluators satisfying the same interface, or run [[alg-midpoint-collocation-for-nonlinear-bvps]] using the pointwise field/boundary values and their exact derivatives required by its residual. Use the residuals of [[def-phase-bordered-multiple-shooting-and-midpoint-collocation]]; in section mode include the constant parameter and affine section row. Missing pointwise/segment evaluation data returns evaluator-unavailable. Use the last finite tuple's first physical state and positive period (and parameter in section mode) as a shooting candidate. Reject a candidate outside $Z$ or a nonrational candidate without a supplied rational proposal; rationalization is only a new candidate, not a trajectory or residual certificate.

All modes propagate evaluator-failure, invalid-endpoint-pair, invalid-trial, singular-jacobian, inconclusive and exhausted-budget statuses. No candidate mode is assumed to succeed from arbitrary data. In particular, the first mode composes the available interval-enclosure provider directly; it does not infer a $C^1$ point evaluator from interval boxes.

**Independent validation:** run [[alg-krawczyk-root-certification]] on $F$ and $Z$ with $C,W,\eta$ and the supplied box budget. First its exact check $WC=I$ must succeed. For every processed subbox $Y\subseteq Z$, let $m_Y$ be its rational midpoint. The residual callback runs the validated shooting jet on $\{m_Y\}$ and returns its $F(m_Y)$ enclosure as $F_0$; the Jacobian callback runs it on $Y$ and returns its $DF(Y)$ enclosure as $J(Y)$. Both append the sound outward section-row enclosures in section mode. This uses the actual midpoint of the current Krawczyk box, even when it differs from the candidate center. A failed query or tube inclusion marks that box unresolved. All interval operations are outward under [[lem-real-interval-arithmetic-preserves-enclosure]]. Retain the complete Krawczyk output partition, including every terminal box and its status. Continue only if the overall Krawczyk status is `complete`, exactly one terminal box $Y$ has status `unique-root`, and every other terminal box has status `root-free`; if there is no such unique box, more than one, or any existence-only/unresolved box, return inconclusive. Let $X_Y$ and $\Theta_Y$ be the physical-state and period projections of the unique-root box, and include $\Lambda_Y$ in section mode. Form $Q_Y=(X_Y\times\Lambda_Y)\times\{I_{d+p}\}\times\Theta_Y$ in section mode, or $Q_Y=X_Y\times\{I_d\}\times\Theta_Y$ in fixed-parameter mode. Check $Q_Y$ is contained in the supplied augmented tube and query the same sound range provider for its augmented field enclosure. Divide the first $d$ coordinates outward by the positive interval $\Theta_Y$ to obtain an interval box containing $f(X_Y,\Lambda_Y)$ (or $f(X_Y)$ in fixed-parameter mode). Require at least one component interval to exclude zero; if inclusion, query or division fails, or no component excludes zero, return inconclusive. Finally require a successful full-box jet run on $Y$ to enclose the entire trajectory and monodromy; a failed query or tube check returns inconclusive.

Return `validated-root` only for such a box $Y$, and report it as the output box together with the complete terminal partition, the actual midpoint residual enclosure, Jacobian enclosure, inverse witness, strict inequalities, field component excluding zero, trajectory tube and monodromy enclosure. The complete partition proves that $Y$ contains the only zero in the original box $Z$. If subdivision was used the output box is $Y$, not the original larger $Z$. Otherwise return inconclusive or the precise finite candidate failure status. Candidate midpoints and correction residuals never replace the independently validated callback enclosures.

Input a positive integer $n$, a nonempty complex matrix family $\mathcal M$ enclosed entrywise by finite dyadic real/imaginary rectangles, a dyadic center matrix $M_0$, a certified dyadic bound $\delta_A\ge\sup_{M\in\mathcal M}\|M-M_0\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$, and a simple positively oriented strictly convex polygon $\Gamma$ with dyadic vertices and filled interior $P$. Supply the dyadic disk cover and point preconditioners required by [[alg-complex-resolvent-cover-validator]], a positive integer $N$ for midpoint subdivisions of each edge, a positive integer $K_\pi$ for the arctangent series, and a finite arithmetic budget. The family may be the monodromy block of a validated shooting jet; no correlation between matrix entries is required. A complex rectangle here is the product of one closed dyadic real interval and one closed dyadic imaginary interval for each matrix entry.

1. Write the ordered dyadic vertices as $v_0,\ldots,v_{r-1}$, with indices modulo $r$. Require $r\ge3$, pairwise distinct vertices, and, for every $i$ and every $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$, the exact rational determinant $\operatorname{Im}(\overline{(v_{i+1}-v_i)}(v_k-v_i))>0$. Each directed edge is then an exposed edge of the convex hull; since there are $r$ such edges and $r$ distinct vertices, they form its simple counterclockwise boundary. If any test fails, output `inconclusive`. Then run the resolvent-cover validator on every edge for the entire family. If any segment is uncovered, an outward inequality is not strict, or no finite upper bound $M_R$ on $\|(zI-M)^{-1}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$ is returned, output `inconclusive`.
2. Subdivide each oriented edge $e_j=b_j-a_j$ into $N$ equal parts, with rational midpoints $z_{jk}=a_j+(k+1/2)e_j/N$. By exact rational complex elimination, compute $R^0_{jk}=(z_{jk}I-M_0)^{-1}$; a singular center matrix or an incomplete operation returns `inconclusive`. For each rational complex entry $a+ib$ of $R^0_{jk}$, use rational square-root bisection to find an upper bound for $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, then sum row bounds to obtain $b_{jk}\ge\|R^0_{jk}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$. Use the same bisection to obtain $s_j\ge|e_j|$. If the finite budget does not produce these rational bounds, return `inconclusive`.
3. Form the exact center midpoint sum
$$S_0=\sum_j\frac{e_j}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\operatorname{tr}R^0_{jk},$$
and the outward error allowance
$$E=\frac{n M_R^2}{2N}\sum_j|e_j|^2+\frac{n M_R\delta_A}{N}\sum_{j,k}s_jb_{jk}.$$
The first term uses the exact rational squared modulus of each rational edge; the second uses the rational upper edge length $s_j$. The first term bounds midpoint quadrature error; the second bounds replacing each family resolvent by the center resolvent. All sums and products are exact rationals; if a required rational square-root upper bound is unavailable, return `inconclusive`.
4. Enclose $\pi$ using $\pi=4\arctan(1)$ and the alternating partial sum $4\sum_{k=0}^{K_\pi-1}(-1)^k/(2k+1)$ with tail radius $4/(2K_\pi+1)$. Require a positive lower endpoint. Using exact rational endpoint arithmetic, enclose $S_0/(2\pi i)$ and inflate its real and imaginary intervals by $E/(2\pi_{\rm low})$; call the resulting rectangle $I$.
5. Choose an integer $c$ and return `certified-count(c)` only if $0\le c\le n$, $\operatorname{Re}I\subset(c-1/2,c+1/2)$, $\operatorname{Im}I\subset(-1/2,1/2)$, and $0\in\operatorname{Im}I$. Otherwise return `inconclusive`. This operation counts roots with algebraic multiplicity in $\operatorname{int}P$ for every matrix in the supplied family; it does not classify a cluster touching the unit circle as stable or unstable.

For a simple separated multiplier, an optional left/right-conditioned finite enclosure may also be reported using [[lem-separated-simple-floquet-multiplier-perturbation-bound]]. The contour count remains the required path for clusters or unresolved individual eigenvectors.

The matrix family may be taken from the monodromy block of [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]]. Resolvent bounds use the complex infinity norm [[def-complex-infinity-matrix-norm]] and its product inequality [[lem-complex-infinity-matrix-norm-submultiplicative]]; the boundary cover is interpreted by [[thm-complex-resolvent-cover-validator-soundness]]. Root counting uses [[thm-argument-principle-null-homologous-cycle]], the inside/outside polygon index [[lem-positive-convex-polygon-winding-index]], and the determinant derivative [[thm-determinant-differential-and-jacobis-formula]]. The root multiplicities are those of the characteristic polynomial by [[thm-complex-polynomial-has-exactly-degree-many-roots-counted-with-multiplicity]]. The rational $\pi$ enclosure uses [[thm-principal-inverse-tangent-calculus]] and [[thm-alternating-series-test]].
